correctness.rationale: For every nonzero \(\omega\), Cayley–Hamilton gives \(\mathcal E(\omega)=\det(B)\|\omega\|^2/(\omega^\top B\omega)\). For Gaussian sketches the unit direction is uniform and \(\int_0^{2\pi}d\theta/(\lambda\cos^2\theta+\mu\sin^2\theta)=2\pi/\sqrt{\lambda\mu}\); for sign sketches the only two rays have Rayleigh quotients \(s\pm b\). Exact monotonicity over \(0\le|b|\le(\lambda-\mu)/2\) yields both attainable endpoints and equality classes. Comparison with \(\sqrt{\det B}\) gives the crossover; a trigonometric measure calculation yields the bad-orientation frequency and asymptotic law. The standalone verifier passed 7,904 exact-rational algebraic checks and 1,123 numerical checks. Finite checks are supplemental, not proofs.

value.rationale: A mathematically meaningful randomized low-rank approximation decision—Gaussian versus inexpensive sign probes—can reverse solely under right-singular basis rotation at fixed singular spectrum. The exact sign-probe approximation factor is as low as \(2\kappa^2/(\kappa^2+1)<2\) and as high as \((\kappa^2+1)/2\), while Gaussian has \(\kappa\); the exact rotation frontier and adverse-orientation measure quantify when each distribution wins. These structural boundaries are not mere renamings of the standard stochastic range-projection bounds and may inform sketch-distribution selection and robustness tests.
